item.title: New York Jets owner Woody Johnson to be honored at Tunnel to Towers gala for decade-long partnership
item.description: New York Jets owner Woody Johnson is being honored at Tunnel to Towers' 2026 gala for his more than decade-long partnership with the organization.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX — New York Jets owner Woody Johnson is being honored at Tunnel to Towers' annual gala being held later this year for his decade-long partnership with the organization.

Tunnel to Towers, founded in 2001 to aid 9/11 first responders, veterans and their families, has been providing mortgage-free smart homes to disabled servicemen as well as housing for homeless veterans.

Johnson's philanthropy with Tunnel to Towers began in 2014 when he donated $1 million to the group's Building for America’s Bravest program.

TUNNEL TO TOWERS ANNOUNCES 'STEEL ACROSS AMERICA' TOUR TO MARK 25 YEARS SINCE 9/11 ATTACKS

Last month, Johnson and Tunnel to Towers surprised Command Sergeant Major William "Bud" McElroy with a new mortgage-free smart home.

"Tunnel to Towers' extraordinary work is a constant reminder of the importance of honoring the memory of the heroes who demonstrated courage and made the ultimate sacrifice for this country," Johnson told Fox News Digital. "Over the past two decades they have channeled grief into action, and it's a privilege to be recognized by such an honorable group."

MASSIVE PIECE OF 9/11 HISTORY MAKES STUNNING 10,500-MILE JOURNEY ACROSS AMERICA

"Woody Johnson has been standing with our families for more than a decade, and he's never once asked for anything in return," Tunnel to Towers Chairman and CEO Frank Siller said in a statement. "Because of Woody, his family, and the Betty Wood Johnson Foundation, six catastrophically injured veterans are living in specially adapted smart homes today, and first responder families across this country are keeping their homes."

"My brother Stephen ran toward people who needed him without asking what it would cost him — Woody has been doing the same thing for twelve years. There's no one more deserving of the Follow the Footsteps Award, which we will be presenting to him at our gala in December," Siller added.

CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS

The gala honoring Johnson will take place in December.

Johnson previously served as the U.S. ambassador to the United Kingdom during the first Trump administration and is a founding trustee of the 9/11 Memorial & Museum.

item.title: Supreme Court chief justice praises outgoing Smithsonian leader who was under pressure from Trump admin
item.description: John Roberts praised Lonnie Bunch's Smithsonian leadership as the secretary retired amid mounting Trump administration pressure over museum exhibits.
item.content:encoded:
Supreme Court Chief Justice John Roberts praised the outgoing head of the Smithsonian Institution on Tuesday after the official came under fire from President Donald Trump's administration.

Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie Bunch, 73, announced plans to retire this week after more than a year of tension with the White House over how U.S. history is presented at his institution. The Trump administration released a July report earlier this summer laying out its criticisms of the National Museum of American History in particular.

Roberts, who serves as the chancellor of the Smithsonian, hailed Bunch on his departure, saying he "pursued excellence in the telling of our nation’s story" and that the Smithsonian had "benefited greatly from his wisdom, vision and leadership."

FORMER DEMOCRATIC STAFFERS, DEI LEADERS SHAPE SMITHSONIAN LEADERSHIP AMID POLITICAL FIRESTORM

Prior to his departure, Bunch had pushed back internally on criticism from the White House. The July report argued that the Smithsonian had become "subject to institutional capture by a radical, activist ideology that is fundamentally opposed to telling the noble, honest story of the great country we know and love."

Bunch responded with an internal email to staff members, acknowledging that there is "room for improvement," but arguing the report was "not a fair characterization of the work and totality of the National Museum of American History."

TRUMP ORDERS SIGNS OUTSIDE SMITHSONIAN MUSEUM AMID ROW OVER ITS DEPICTION OF AMERICAN HISTORY

"At the Smithsonian, our work is driven by scholarship, accuracy and an uncompromising commitment to tell the fullness of America's story. As public servants and the keepers of this institution, we are charged with helping a nation find understanding, hope and clarity and as part of that duty, we are dedicated to excellence, reflection and growth," he wrote.

Bunch appears to have relented to pressure after the latest move by the White House, which saw Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and White House Domestic Policy Council Director Vince Haley warn that the Smithsonian could lose access to artifacts and grants from the federal government if it continues with its current leadership.

SMITHSONIAN'S TAXPAYER FUNDS FACE CHOPPING BLOCK AS GOP DEMANDS ACCOUNTABILITY FOR 'WOKE' HISTORY

Burgum and Haley wrote a letter to Congress last week laying out concerns about ideological capture and potential misconduct among the Smithsonian's leadership.

"The administration has recently uncovered evidence that the Smithsonian leadership's institutional culture may have resulted in significant violations of Federal antidiscrimination law, including creating a hostile work environment and engaging in practices that classify individuals and allocate opportunities, funding and other benefits on the basis of race, ethnicity and other protected characteristics," the letter read.

item.title: From intelligence sharing to missile defense, how Israel's partnership protects American security
item.description: Joint strikes on Iran, intelligence sharing and missile defense reveal why vilifying Israel in 2026 could prove self-defeating for the U.S.
item.content:encoded:
The anti-Israel sentiment that has been gathering momentum in the U.S. since Oct. 7, 2023, is nationally self-sabotaging. Americans should understand the ties between the U.S. and Israel are mutually beneficial and a significant portion of America’s security can be linked directly to this vital relationship.

After Oct. 7, 2023, when the terrorist organization Hamas invaded Israel from Gaza and slaughtered over 1200 victims and kidnapped another 251, the streets and campuses of America exploded with protests against the victim – Israel – while endorsing the murderous terrorist organization – Hamas. This century has never seen such a widespread response that was sympathetic to terrorists and not to victims.

Fast-forward to over six months ago when the U.S. and Israel conducted joint strikes on Iranian military targets with the goal of stopping the Iranian regime from having a nuclear weapon. With on-again, off-again ceasefires and deals that have not yet resulted in a lasting peace or a change in status regarding Iran’s pursuit of nuclear weapons, some Americans are now accusing Israel of pressuring the U.S. to serve Israel’s interests, blaming the Jewish state for dragging the U.S. into an extended overseas war, using American resources to defend Israel and putting U.S. troops in harm’s way, to name only a few.

‘NO JEWS, NO NEWS’ STRIKES AGAIN AS SELECTIVE COVERAGE OF THE 'UNSETTLERS' FUELS ANTI-ISRAEL ANGER

Vilifying Israel is becoming normalized in 2026 by both American politicians and voters. Some Democratic political candidates and representatives are associating themselves with the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA). Being anti-Israel is a DSA core value; in fact, Gaza has become a central issue for the organization. In 2025, the DSA adopted a resolution making a member’s support for Israel’s right to defend itself an expellable offense. In the same year, opposition to the idea of Jews having a homeland in the historic land of Israel (Zionism) was adopted as an organizational principle.

American left-wing politicians are not just paying lip-service to the DSA, they are aligning themselves with this organization that supports sanctioning America’s strongest ally in the Middle East while opposing American sanctions of oppressive and tyrannical governments such as those found in Cuba, North Korea, Iran and Venezuela. 

And what of the general U.S. population? An April 2026 Pew Research Center poll found "60% of U.S. adults have an unfavorable view of Israel." 

SIGN UP FOR ANTISEMITISM EXPOSED NEWSLETTER

Is antisemitism behind this anti-Israel phenomenon? Absolutely – it plays a central role for the anti-Israel fanatics. But most Americans are not fanatics and in a world of social media lies, many are simply unsure of the truth, a logical byproduct of what they consume on legacy news media and social media.

After the United Nations General Assembly voted to create a Jewish state in late 1947 and Israel’s subsequent proclamation of independence in May 1948, America supported Israel by being the first country to recognize the fledgling nation. The American-Israeli relationship grew over the following decades, and Israel, the only democracy in the Middle East, was seen as a vital strategic asset to America in the face of Soviet influence in the region. In a May 1968 article in the LA Times, American social philosopher Eric Hoffer wrote, "…at this moment, Israel is our only reliable and unconditional ally. We can rely more on Israel than Israel can rely on us."

In the 1990s, the two countries developed a deep strategic cooperation and intelligence sharing relationship that continues today. According to the Federal Newswire, although Israel is America’s largest recipient of foreign aid, the return on investment far exceeds the cost. 

For example, in 2016, the U.S. agreed to provide Israel $3.8 billion per year for ten years. Analysis shows the U.S. receives, in return, approximately $48 billion in annual benefits from this agreement. Benefits to the U.S. include Israel testing U.S. weapons systems in combat, providing intelligence to the U.S. (covering threats from Iran, its terror proxies, and the weapons each can employ against Americans), and aiding in the development of defensive missile systems – many of which have been used in the current conflict with Iran to protect American bases and allies overseas.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

The FBI opened an overseas post in Tel Aviv in the mid-1990s and the FBI has had a presence there ever since. From 2020 to 2024, I was assigned to Israel as an FBI Supervisory Special Agent focusing on counterterrorism matters with our Israeli security partners. 

I personally experienced the two-way exchange of intelligence with Israeli police, Shin Bet and other security services on all matters related to threats faced by both countries. I was in Israel for the horrific global event of Oct. 7 and worked around the clock with U.S. and Israeli counterparts to gather intelligence on the missing victims (including Americans), seek justice against the Hamas perpetrators and provide comfort and answers to the victims’ families. The cooperation between the two nations could not be stronger.

I have previously written about how Israel is the "canary in the coal mine" when it comes to terrorism – "Israel’s experience with terrorism is often a preview of what the West can expect to see within its borders." America is safer because of Israel and – because of my official FBI tour in Israel – I can testify to this truth. The relationship between Israel and the U.S. is not based solely on shared values, history, or political support – it is also built on a deep mutual security interest that provides tangible benefits to the American people.

Hoffer concluded his aforementioned 1968 LA Times article with the following ominous warning, "I have a premonition that will not leave me; as it goes with Israel so will it go with all of us. Should Israel perish, the Holocaust will be upon us all." 

Americans need to realize the true quid pro quo of the U.S.- Israeli alliance before concluding Israel is a bad actor. U.S. politicians and voters should recognize that Americans are safer on our shores because of Israel. As Hoffer implied 58 years ago, if Israel’s existence is endangered or this alliance with America fails, it threatens us all.

item.title: All Elite Wrestling to hold special 'Rebel Heart' episode to benefit Tanea Brooks, who is battling ALS
item.description: AEW's "Rebel Heart" edition of "Dynamite" features a stacked card with Will Ospreay, Darby Allin, and Kyle Fletcher to honor Tanea Brooks' ALS fight.
item.content:encoded:
All Elite Wrestling (AEW) will hold a special edition of "Dynamite" on Wednesday to benefit pro wrestler Tanea Brooks, known as Rebel, who is battling ALS.

"Rebel Heart" will take place at the Akins Ford Arena in Athens, Georgia. AEW and the rest of the pro wrestling world have been in full support of Brooks since she announced her diagnosis back in May. Stars from all promotions have promoted the "Rebel Heart" T-shirts and have performed the ALS Ice Bucket Challenge to raise money and awareness for the awful disease.

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK

AEW and Ring of Honor (ROH) owner Tony Khan spoke about the show in August after ROH’s Death Before Dishonor in Philadelphia.

"Rebel’s been a great friend to all of us and a great part of AEW from the very beginning," he said. "We haven’t seen Rebel on AEW TV in a long time but it’s going to be great to have an episode of AEW TV dedicated to Rebel, fighting this terrible disease, ALS. AEW ‘Rebel Heart’ next month is going to be raising money to fight ALS and it’s in honor of Rebel.

"We all care for her very much and she’s very much a part of the AEW family. Even though she’s not on TV every week, you can believe everyone’s got Rebel in their hearts and we’ll be thinking about Rebel every week."

Brooks announced her diagnosis on May 1.

"The doctors have diagnosed me with terminal ALS," she said in a video. "There is not a lot of research behind ALS, and we don’t know how long I have. But it explains why I have trouble walking and talking, and all my functions will soon decline.

"But now we can prepare for the future and what is to come. And I want to say thank you."

Brooks joined AEW in 2019, initially as a backstage and stylist role before appearing on-screen in 2020 with Britt Baker as her personal makeup artists. She had a few matches before suffering an injury.

She got started in pro wrestling with Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA) in 2013 and made appearances for Ohio Valley Wrestling, Stardom and briefly in WWE.

The "Rebel Heart" card is stacked.

Will Ospreay will take on David Finlay in an AEW World Championship elimination match, Darby Allin and Steven Borden take on Mark Davis and Josh Alexander in a tag team bout, the AEW World Trios Championship will be on the line as Swerve Strickland, Kofi and Austin Creed take on Orange Cassidy, Kyle O’Reily and Roderick Strong, a women’s trios match is set between Maya World, Hyan and Thunder Rosa and Persephone, Baker and Hikaru Shida and the Young Bucks take on Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight in a tables match.

Brooks is also expected to be on the show with Baker in a segment called "The Waiting Room." Persephone and Shida are anticipated to be featured.

item.title: Ben Shelton takes down Carlos Alcaraz to earn the biggest win of his career in latest US Open match ever
item.description: Ben Shelton defeated Carlos Alcaraz in a five-set thriller at Arthur Ashe Stadium, snapping the Spaniard's 18-match Grand Slam winning streak.
item.content:encoded:
It may have happened during a quarter-final match, and it may have taken place while most of the country was asleep, but Ben Shelton officially became the face of American men's tennis on Wednesday morning at the US Open.

After four hours and 28 minutes of war, Shelton secured his victory over seven-time major champion Carlos Alcaraz 6-7 (5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 (10-7) at 3:33 a.m. in New York, making it the longest match in the Grand Slam's history when the clock ticked past 2:50 a.m.

By punching his ticket into the US Open semifinal for the second consecutive year, he guaranteed that the United States will be represented in Sunday's final as he'll take on fellow American Francis Tiafoe on Friday in the semis.

GROUP OF INFLUENCERS FORCES PAUSE DURING US OPEN MATCH WITH CRINGEWORTHY PHOTOSHOOT IN SUITE

An American man has not won a Grand Slam title since Andy Roddick took down Juan Carlos Ferrero at the 2003 US Open.

Shelton certainly had the crowd on his side throughout the match, and admitted that he fed off of the American fans in New York.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"It’s always about the people in the crowd, whether it’s my coaches and my team over there, all my family and friends over here, or the city of New York," Shelton said during his on-court interview following the match. "They showed up tonight till 3 a.m. with USA chats until the very end, that’s what kept me going, and that’s what got me this win tonight.

"I’m just hoping my best friend and my sister over there don’t have to be at work at 6 a.m. in three hours."

LADIES AT THE US OPEN WERE CAUGHT ON CAMERA TAKING NOTICE OF A SHIRTLESS CARLOS ALCARAZ

Shelton's heroics on Arthur Ashe Stadium on Tuesday night and into Wednesday morning snapped Alcaraz's 18-match winning streak in Grand Slam tournaments. As expected, Alcaraz made life tough for Shelton at pivotal points throughout the match, but the Spaniard's 53 unforced errors proved to be a critical difference in the end.

Shelton's serve, the strongest weapon in his repertoire, was on full display as he secured seven aces and just two double faults throughout the five-set thriller. The victory marked Shelton's first time defeating Alcaraz in his career, with the Spaniard previously holding a 3-0 record against the Florida native, with the two last meeting at Roland Garros in 2025.

item.title: Weight regain after obesity drugs tied to higher odds of suicidal thoughts in observational study
item.description: Weight-loss drug users who regained weight had 4.2 times higher odds of suicidal ideation, according to a study analyzing data from over 27,000 adults.
item.content:encoded:
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

Adults who reported using prescription weight-loss medication in the last year had higher rates of depression, mental-health counseling, suicidal thoughts and suicide-related behaviors compared to people who did not take the drugs, according to an observational study.

The research, conducted at Asan Medical Center in South Korea, analyzed data from 27,741 adults (10,908 men and 16,833 women).

Of these participants, 846 had been taking prescription medications for weight control during the previous year, while 26,895 did not take them.

OZEMPIC USERS MAY BE MAKING A MAJOR WEIGHT-LOSS MISTAKE, NEW STUDY SUGGESTS

The weight-loss drug users were 1.9 times more likely to experience depression and twice as likely to seek mental health counseling.

They were also 2.7 times more likely to have suicidal thoughts and 1.7 times more likely to make a suicide attempt.

The associations were stronger among those using the medications who gained or regained weight.

"The tendency for depression and suicide-related indicators to increase as weight rebounds after using weight-loss drugs may reflect not only the neuropsychiatric effects of the drugs themselves, but also a complex interplay of psychological and social factors associated with failed weight control," the research team wrote in the study.

PATIENTS TAKING WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS OFTEN MAKE 5 CRITICAL MISTAKES, DOCTOR WARNS

The findings were published in the Korean Journal of Family Practice on Aug. 23.

Bonnie Mitchell, a licensed professional clinical counselor in California, noted that this was an observational, cross-sectional study.

"It shows a correlation between weight-loss drug use and self-reported mental health symptoms, but it cannot prove causation," she told Fox News Digital. "It does not demonstrate that weight-loss medications directly induce depression or suicidal thoughts."

The data was collected between 2013 and 2022.

"During most of this period, modern GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists used for weight loss (such as high-dose semaglutide/Wegovy or tirzepatide/Zepbound/Mounjaro) were either not yet on the market or had very limited real world uptake in South Korea," Mitchell said.

WHEN IS A MENTAL HEALTH CRISIS TOO SEVERE FOR TELEHEALTH? WARNING SIGNS FAMILIES SHOULDN'T IGNORE

"The study sample captures older anti-obesity agents historically prescribed in South Korea during that decade, including phentermine, diethylpropion, phendimetrazine, topiramate and orlistat."

Central nervous system stimulants – including phentermine-based drugs – have been shown to carry risks of anxiety, mood changes and insomnia, the counselor noted.

"The study highlighted a striking sub finding that found users who gained weight despite taking the medication had 4.2 times higher odds of suicidal ideation compared to non-users," Mitchell noted.

Weight regain or perceived "failure" in weight management can trigger profound guilt, shame, helplessness and psychological distress, according to the expert.

"Individuals with severe obesity have higher baseline rates of depression, anxiety and body dysmorphia," Mitchell said. "A cross-sectional survey cannot separate pre-existing mental health struggles from new symptoms that arose after starting a medication."

More research is needed to determine whether weight-loss medications themselves affect mental health, or whether depression and other symptoms are related to factors such as obesity or difficulties losing weight.

The researchers also need to determine whether mental health risks differ between specific weight-loss drugs.

NEW WEIGHT-LOSS COMPOUND MELTS FAT WITHOUT CURBING APPETITE — AND PRESERVES MUSCLE

"Even though GLP-1 clinical trials show low absolute risk, the FDA’s product labels for chronic weight management drugs (like Wegovy and Zepbound) include warnings to monitor for mood changes," Mitchell noted.

She recommends that a physician conducts a baseline mental health history before prescribing new weight-loss medications, evaluating past or current depression, bipolar disorder, or history of suicidal ideation or behavior.

"Doctors can inform patients and caregivers about potential mood changes so they know what to watch for," Mitchell said. "The next important step for ongoing monitoring would be to schedule check-ins at 4- to 8-week intervals during dose escalation, to evaluate both physiological progress and psychological well-being."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Patients should contact their healthcare provider immediately if they notice new or worsening depressive symptoms, including the following.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"Any active suicidal thoughts require immediate emergency medical care," Mitchell advised.

"If a patient develops emergent depression or suicidal ideation during treatment, clinicians should discontinue the weight-loss medication and connect the patient with psychiatric support."

Eli Lilly, manufacturer of the tirzepatide weight-loss medication Zepbound, explicitly mentions "depression or thoughts of suicide" in its safety information.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"You should pay attention to changes in your mood, behaviors, feelings or thoughts," the website reads.

It further advises patients to contact a healthcare provider if mental health changes are "new, worse or worry you."

On Lilly's medical-information site, the company says that after reviewing clinical trials and medical reports, "no increased risk" of suicidal ideation or psychiatric adverse effects was identified.

Novo Nordisk, manufacturer of the semaglutide weight-loss medication Wegovy, states in its trials that less than 1% of participants experienced suicidal ideation or behavior during treatment. It also says there was "no difference between semaglutide 2.4 mg and placebo."

Fox News Digital reached out to Lilly and Novo Nordisk for comment.

item.title: Flight 93 hero's dad warns 'enemies from within' aim to destroy America at the ballot box
item.description: Todd Beamer's father compared the Michigan Senate race to defending America on 9/11, backing Mike Rogers over Abdul El-Sayed in a fiery appeal.
item.content:encoded:
David Beamer, the father of 9/11 Flight 93 hero Todd Beamer, called on Michigan to "vote American this time," warning that he believes Democratic socialists pose an existential threat to the nation.

Speaking on "America's Newsroom," Tuesday, Beamer compared voting in the upcoming election to defending the country, calling on voters to reject what he described as radical agendas.

"These Democratic socialists are really more closely aligned with domestic terrorists than with our way of life," Beamer said.

EX-DSA MEMBER RIPS ABDUL EL-SAYED AND WARNS FAR-LEFT ADOPTING POLITICS OF FOREIGN TERROR ORG

"The good news is, their weapon of choice is not a bomb or turning an airplane into a guided missile. Their weapon of choice is a ballot," he added.

Beamer's son Todd was among the passengers who fought back against the hijackers on September 11, 2001, rallying fellow passengers to storm the cockpit of United Airlines Flight 93. The plane crashed near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, killing everyone on board, but the passengers’ actions prevented the hijackers from reaching their intended target in Washington, D.C.

‘FIESTA MEXICANA’: EL-SAYED CAMPAIGN PLANS FESTIVE 9/11 WHILE REMEMBRANCE IS MISSING FROM PUBLIC SCHEDULE

Beamer, a Michigan voter, endorsed Mike Rogers in the Senate race over Democratic opponent Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, telling his fellow Michiganders they have a decision to make about the future of their state.

"I'm [going to] vote against those that want to destroy America. I'm [going to] vote for an American, a real Michigan man. His name happens to be Mike Rogers. I want everybody across all the platforms, Democrat, independent, Republican, vote American this time. Don't vote for those who are set about to destroy our [freedoms]," Beamer said.

ROGERS OPENS DOOR TO DEMOCRATIC VOTERS AFTER EL-SAYED’S PRIMARY VICTORY: ‘THERE IS STILL HOPE’

El-Sayed has faced criticism from Rogers over past comments he made regarding the 9/11 terrorist attacks in now-deleted social media posts.

"Today, I mourn the 3K lives, 6K injuries, & infrastructural devastation in NYC, perpetuated ignorantly in the name of my faith. Tomorrow, I'll mourn ~1M lives, millions of injuries, & infrastructural devastation in 3 countries, perpetuated ignorantly in the name of my country," he wrote in a 2021 post first reported by the Washington Free Beacon.

CBS NEWS TAKES HEAT OVER REPORT ON DEM HOPEFUL ABDUL EL-SAYED'S NOW-DELETED 9/11 POSTS

Beamer drew a comparison between the 9/11 attacks and the upcoming election, warning that while the nation was caught unprepared on 9/11, voters today cannot afford to be surprised.

"The other thing that I reflect on about 9/11, that was a surprise attack. We didn't see it coming. We weren't prepared," Beamer said. "Some, like Todd, had to go to battle that day. Others had to rush into buildings to try and save people. We weren't ready for that attack."

LIZ PEEK: MICHIGAN CAN STOP THE SOCIALIST FEVER RAGE — OR WATCH IT SWALLOW THE SENATE

Beamer argued that the threats facing the country have evolved and now include adversaries operating from within. "Our enemies haven't gone away," he said. "They identify themselves as Democratic socialists. Their platform is one that aims to destroy all the values and the foundations of this country that we’ve enjoyed for hundreds of years."

"Well, the good news is, in this upcoming attack, and we know when it starts, early voting starts in a few weeks. That's when this battle begins. We all have the same weapon. I've got a ballot," Beamer concluded.

Fox News Digital reached out to the El-Sayed campaign for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Washington father sues school district for denying religious opt-out for 5th grader from LGBTQ instruction
item.description: Alliance Defending Freedom sued Lake Washington School District after a father says his son learned about gender-change surgery during Pride Month.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE — A Washington father is suing his son’s public school district after he said his 10-year-old was taught about gender surgery during a Pride Month lesson despite the Christian parent previously asking the school to excuse his child from LGBTQ-related instruction.

On Tuesday, Alliance Defending Freedom (ADF), which is representing the father, Konstantin Averkiev, filed a federal lawsuit against Lake Washington School District, alleging officials violated Averkiev’s First and 14th Amendment rights by refusing to provide notice and allow his son to opt out of LGBTQ-related lessons and other school requirements that conflict with his religious beliefs.

The dispute began after Averkiev said he met with his son’s fourth-grade teacher at Henry David Thoreau Elementary School in September 2025 and requested advance notice and an opt-out from lessons involving LGBTQ topics, gender identity or gender transition.

WASHINGTON SCHOOL REMOVES TESTOSTERONE VIALS FROM PRIDE DISPLAY AFTER DISTRICT SAYS THEY WERE NOT APPROVED

According to the complaint, the teacher agreed, but Averkiev subsequently found out his son had been taught a June Pride Month lesson that allegedly included a classroom discussion of gender-change surgery.

The teacher then said he remembered Averkiev’s request and told him he "should have sent the lessons ahead of time," according to messages cited in the lawsuit. However, Averkiev said that the district later rejected nearly all of his broader opt-out requests as his son prepared to enter fifth grade.

The Pride Month presentation, taught to fourth and fifth-grade students, described same-sex attraction, transgender identity and the Stonewall uprising, a series of protests from people who identified as LGBTQ+ against a police raid on June 28, 1969, at the Stonewall Inn in New York City's Greenwich Village, according to materials cited in the complaint.

WATCH: FATHER OF THREE OUTRAGED OVER ADVICE HIS FAMILY RECEIVED AMID TRANS TEACHER FIGHT

Averkiev also alleged the classroom discussion went further than just the slides. His son told him the class had discussed gender-change surgery, meaning the father argues he would not have known the subject was coming even if the school had provided him the presentation in advance.

With his son starting fifth grade, Averkiev, with the help of ADF attorneys, asked the district to excuse his son from LGBTQ-related instruction and requirements, including individual counseling sessions and the use of pronouns that conflict with his religious beliefs, according to ADF.

ADF said the district rejected nearly all of Averkiev’s requests, granting only opt-outs for sex-education curriculum and health surveys, which the legal group noted are already required under Washington state law.

TRUMP DOJ EXPANDS RELIGIOUS LIBERTY PROTECTIONS AFTER MAJOR SUPREME COURT RULINGS

But the legal group maintains that Averkiev’s rights are protected under the First and 14th Amendments, and "extend to every lesson or government-school requirement on his son that would ‘undermin[e] the religious beliefs and practices’ Mr. Averkiev wishes to instill in his son," according to the lawsuit.

"Parents have the fundamental right to direct their children’s religious upbringing and education, even at school," Kate Anderson, ADF senior counsel and director of the ADF Center for Parental Rights, said in a statement. "Washington state officials can’t force parents like Mr. Averkiev to give up that right or accept a burden on their children’s religious upbringing in exchange for the benefit of public education." 

"Our Constitution forbids schools from indoctrinating children with the government’s views on sexuality and gender — hotly debated and sensitive topics — that substantially undermine their religious upbringing," she added.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Averkiev said, "As a parent, I have a right to decide what my son learns about sex and gender at school. He's ten years old. I don't want him to learn about gender-change surgery and using false pronouns." 

"I have repeatedly asked to opt my son out of the school district's LGBTQ instruction. But the district has refused. I am filing this lawsuit, so schools cannot ignore parents like me," he added.

Lake Washington School District declined to comment when reached by Fox News Digital, but said that it follows "all applicable federal and state laws and guidance from the Office of the Superintendent of Public Instruction."

item.title: BROOKE ROLLINS, MONICA CROWLEY: America’s family farms have kept us strong for 250 years
item.description: Round Swamp Farm in East Hampton, N.Y., traces back to John Lester 300 years ago and now anchors the new American Family Farm Legacy 250 Program.
item.content:encoded:
Half a century before America declared independence, John Lester broke soil on a 150-acre plot of land in East Hampton, New York. Little did he know, the next 300 years would see nine generations of his direct descendants cultivate that land. As our young nation took root and endured hardship, so did Round Swamp Farm. Today, Carolyn Lester Snyder carries on the family tradition by growing and selling produce on the property, with the help of her husband, children and grandchildren. They are a living, breathing, working testament to the American Dream and to America’s long legacy of family farming.

This summer, the Trump administration is honoring that glorious inheritance by launching the American Family Farm Legacy 250 Program. In partnership with the National Association of State Departments of Agriculture, the U.S. Department of Agriculture is building on proud traditions established during America’s bicentennial and elevating them into a unified national commitment.

A long chain of uninterrupted family ownership is no small feat. That’s why this program publicly recognizes the inspirational perseverance of multigenerational farm families, from 100-year legacies to the extraordinary handful of patriots who have stewarded their land for 250 years or more.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION EXPANDS 'PRODUCT OF USA' LABEL AS PUSH FOR AMERICAN-RAISED BEEF GROWS

From the Eastern Shore of Maryland to the wooded hills of western Massachusetts, from the South Fork of Long Island to the country roads of rural North Carolina, these farms remind us just how much rural America matters to all of America. Critically, they have sustained us with the food we eat and the clothes on our backs. But even more importantly, they have been the wellspring of our most cherished values and time-honored traditions.

In times of tranquility and times of crisis, these men and women stand in the gap, reaffirming their commitment to the American way of life. To faith and family. To patriotism and civic responsibility. To standing where their mothers and fathers stood. And to remaining steadfast in hope for what’s on the horizon.

STEVE MOORE: POLITICIANS ARE BLAMING THE WRONG VILLAIN FOR AMERICA’S RISING FOOD PRICES

When the first generations of these family farmers planted the seeds of liberty, they laid the foundation for an unrivaled American agricultural might that has only grown stronger across each generation. During droughts and depression, through war and peace, their forebears kept the plows turning, the tractors running and our rich American soil fertile for freedom.

These powerful legacies remind each of us that we are part of a larger story — a story we did not originally author and the ending of which we will not see. Our duty is to honor the magnificent inheritance we’ve been gifted by fighting for the prosperity of American agriculture with every fiber of our being. This is at the heart of the Farmers First agenda we are carrying out across the Trump administration. Empowered by President Donald Trump’s leadership, we are putting our farmers, ranchers and rural communities back at the center of policymaking.

REP ROGER WILLIAMS: 250 YEARS OF HARD WORK PAYS OFF FOR MAIN STREET BUSINESSES

While the American Family Farm Legacy 250 Program is primarily meant to put a spotlight on farms with centuries of continuous operation, it also celebrates the future of American agriculture and the next generation of farmers who dare to take up the noble mantle of stewardship.

After all, America’s success is bound up in theirs. This is what Thomas Jefferson meant when he wrote in 1785, "Cultivators of the earth are the most valuable citizens. They are the most vigorous, the most independent, the most virtuous, and they are tied to their country and wedded to its liberty and interests by the most lasting bands."

The family farms honored by the American Family Farm Legacy 250 Program are bound more closely to our nation than any others. As we continue celebrating America’s 250th birthday, it is only fitting that we salute the families whose grit, sacrifice and stewardship have fed our nation, strengthened our communities and preserved our agricultural heritage across generations.

Five of those families joined us on the National Mall this summer, and we are eager to visit more in person in the coming months. President Trump has made restoring pride in America’s history a national priority, and together, we are ensuring our farmers receive the recognition and support that they deserve.

item.title: George Bush welcomes top officials to his home state for 9/11 remembrance on 25th anniversary of attacks
item.description: George W. Bush and Condoleezza Rice will share their reflections on 9/11's legacy at a Dallas event ahead of the 25th anniversary of the attacks.
item.content:encoded:
DALLAS — George W. Bush was president during the Sept. 11, 2001 terror attacks, and he is marking the 25th anniversary of the day that changed America forever by hosting a solemn remembrance event in his home state.

The event, called "A Legacy of Service: America at the 25th Anniversary of 9/11," will take place at the George W. Bush Presidential Center in Dallas, Texas, and kicks off at 6:30 p.m. local time on Wednesday evening.

It will feature a conversation between former President Bush and former Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice, who "will share their reflections on the legacy and meaning of 9/11—how the day changed the country, how it continues to shape American life, and how the call to serve remains as urgent as ever," according to the webpage for the event.

9/11 MUSEUM CEO REFLECTS ON LASTING IMPACT OF TERROR ATTACKS AS AMERICA MARKS 250TH BIRTHDAY

A moderated discussion between General Dan Caine, the current chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and former Deputy National Security Advisor J.D. Crouch, who served in that role under Bush from 2005 to 2007, is also part of the program.

Melissa Stockwell, a two-time Paralympic triathlete and Army veteran who was awarded a Purple Heart and Bronze Star after losing her leg in Iraq, is a featured guest. So is Jared Lyons, a Navy veteran and CEO of Student Veterans of America.

MASSIVE WORLD TRADE CENTER STEEL BEAM ARRIVES AT WEST POINT, UNITING 9/11 HEROES WITH GENERATION SENT TO WAR

"Together, these conversations will offer a thoughtful, elevated reflection on a defining moment in American history and on the enduring commitment to service that continues to strengthen the nation," the webpage for the event says.

As part of the 25th anniversary commemoration, Bush painted 16 works of art that "reflect on the courage, sacrifice, and resilience that emerged from one of the most defining moments in American history," that will be displayed at Freedom Hall at the Bush Museum through September.

Bush was known for his painting hobby when he occupied the White House and in the years after he left office.

The Bush Presidential Center has also invited the public to join in a moment of remembrance on Friday morning, alongside local first responders.

Bush was president on Sept. 11, 2001, and was visiting an elementary school for an education event when he was informed that America was under attack. He first used the phrase "war on terrorism" on Sept. 16, 2001, and officially declared a campaign during a Sept. 20, 2001 joint address to Congress, which kicked off the 20-year war on terror.

He was elected for a second term in 2004 and retired to Texas with his wife Laura, and the two have maintained a relatively low profile.

item.title: A year after Charlie Kirk's murder, some comics are calling out jokes about his death
item.description: After initial grief following Charlie Kirk’s murder, less than a year later and the mainstream comedy world would resort to treating the event as material for a comedy roast.
item.content:encoded:
As the one-year mark since the murder of Charlie Kirk approaches this week, some comedians are calling out fellow comics for their jokes and reactions following the assassination of the conservative activist.

In May, Pete Davidson made a joke about Kirk’s assassination during Netflix’s "The Roast of Kevin Hart" in Los Angeles. Yet even in today’s "anything goes" style in the world of entertainment, Davidson’s joke shocked some fellow humorists. 

Talking about fellow comedian Tony Hinchcliffe, Davidson said on May 10, 2026, "Tony reminds me of Charlie Kirk in that he’s definitely been on camera letting a guy unload in his throat."

ROGAN TELLS ‘TRAITOR’ COMEDIANS CONDEMNING THE KEVIN HART ROAST TO ‘F--- ALL THE WAY OFF’

"I watched it, and the reaction, you know, was like a giant groan, which is not what you want as a comedian," performer and comedy writer Michael Loftus told Fox News Digital. "With Davidson, it’s like, ‘My reputation precedes me. I’m daring, I’m brash. I’ll say anything.’ Well, yeah, I’ll say anything about the guy who is not going to punch me back. You’re certainly brave about the guy who’s not in the room."

Loftus, who met Kirk years ago at the nonpartisan political convention Politicon in Los Angeles, said that as a comedian, he’s "all about freedom of speech and the First Amendment," but described those who made jokes about Kirk as "just absolute cowards."

Comedian Bryan Callen told Fox News Digital that satire has long helped keep rulers in check and prevented people from taking themselves too seriously.

"You’re reminded that we’re all going to die someday," he said, explaining how comedy acts as a social equalizer and brings people together by highlighting human flaws.

"But then there’s something called good taste and compassion and things that just don’t make you laugh because somebody was killed," he said. "When something terrible happens publicly, and you see somebody killed in front of their children and their wife, I think we need a button that says, ‘Wait, hold on…’"

The joke generated backlash on social media. 

DISNEY UNDER FIRE AS ABC GRAPPLES WITH ANOTHER JIMMY KIMMEL CONTROVERSY

Jimmy Kimmel ran into trouble days after the assassination as well. The "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" host was suspended by ABC after the comedian criticized the political reaction to Kirk’s assassination and erroneously implied the suspect in the case was a MAGA supporter. 

On Sept. 15, 2025, he said, "We hit some new lows over the weekend with the MAGA gang desperately trying to characterize this kid who murdered Charlie Kirk as anything other than one of them and doing everything they can to score political points from it."

DISNEY ACCUSES TRUMP'S FCC OF ATTEMPTING TO 'SUPPRESS SPEECH' WITH LICENSE RENEWAL INVESTIGATION

But ABC brought his show back less than a week after suspending it, following a controversy involving Disney, FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, the Trump administration, ABC and its affiliates. The episode raised questions about whether government and political pressure exerted through broadcasters and regulators could influence what a comedian can say.

Meanwhile, more than 400 entertainment figures, including Jennifer Aniston, Tom Hanks and Meryl Streep, signed an ACLU-backed open letter supporting Kimmel and warning against threats to free speech.

Others, like comic book writer and horror novelist Gretchen Felker-Martin, who posted incendiary comments about Kirk right after his death, didn’t have such support.

Felker-Martin had her "Red Hood" comic series canceled by DC Comics. The comic book publisher said posts or public comments that could be viewed as promoting hostility or violence were "inconsistent with DC's standards of conduct."

For his part, comedian Trevor Noah turned his commentary about Kirk's death into a discussion of gun control rather than the debate over censorship and speech.

Meanwhile, the sitcom "South Park" became part of the debate. The show had parodied Kirk just weeks before his death, and Kirk embraced the joke, calling it a "badge of honor." But after his murder, Comedy Central pulled the episode from its cable rotation.

Loftus, who noted he’s been doing stand-up for years, said he often sees comedians, for example, have no problem making fun of Christianity when they’re actually joking about members of a religion known for turning the other cheek, which he said Kirk practiced.

"I would love to see Pete Davidson’s material on Islam. He’s such a brave and incredibly thoughtful performer that surely he has some jokes about Islam," he said. "Oh, your Charlie Kirk stuff — yes, very edgy and brave of you. But surely there are some jokes about Muhammad."

Fox News Digital reached out to Davidson for comment. 

Loftus argued that many in Hollywood who opposed Kirk's beliefs haven't gone back to Kirk's own material, which Loftus described as thoughtful and well-presented, with Kirk delivering his arguments with a smile and a warm heart.

Callen described Kirk as a formidable intellect who could defend his positions and talk to people with whom he disagreed because he had studied their arguments more than his opponents had. Following Kirk, he said, never meant you had to be of one particular political persuasion.

"What he would always say is, ‘If people stop talking and stop debating in good faith, very bad things happen.’ So, I think Charlie Kirk, in many ways, was reminding us that this — our country and its freedoms — took a long time to build, and so much of us now, it’s very easy to define what you’re against, and it’s actually very easy to build a following and clicks by taking a strong side and amplifying your monologue. But Kirk didn’t ignore nuance or having a discussion," Callen said.

"Again, he had the respect to read the people he disagreed with and not just read, but try to understand from their perspective," he said.

"He could tell you exactly what the Old and New Testament was, how it contributes to the very lives we live today. Not many people can do that. That takes a lot of effort," Callen added. "He earned his point of view. He earned it. It wasn’t based on attitude. It was based on research and thought, and immersing himself in the best that’s been taught and said."

Loftus said that the message of common sense will ultimately succeed.

"The message that Charlie was sending out into the universe will certainly prevail. It’s just a matter of, you know, how long is it going to take and how much suffering will it take to get there?"

item.title: Prince George follows Prince William's footsteps at Eton in a changing royal world: experts
item.description: Prince George arrived at Eton College with Prince William and Kate Middleton beaming beside him, marking a major milestone for the future king.
item.content:encoded:
Prince George is following in his father's footsteps by attending Eton College and royal experts are calling it a very different royal world.

"A new successful chapter for the future heir to the throne. His great-grandmother would be tickled pink. It’s four years to the day, she passed. No doubt he’ll settle in well and master all the skills of kingship," Helena Chard, British broadcaster and photographer, told Fox News Digital.

Chard added, "A buoyant Prince George arrived at Eton with the grounding presence of his chuffed supportive parents. He beamed to cameras fully aware of the drill. A brief photo-call, picture release and a hope that his education will take place away from public eyes. Simon Henderson welcomed Prince George to Eton, telling him, 'Welcome. Good Luck. Enjoy it.'"

PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE WON’T ‘HIJACK’ PRINCE GEORGE’S HISTORIC ETON DEBUT, ROYAL EXPERT SAYS

Chard told Fox News Digital that Prince George's classmates could turn into paparazzi, but it's highly unlikely.

"His friends could be the new paparazzi with their phones at the ready. However, my hunch is his peers are of similar high profile ilk, unfazed by celebrity and royalty," she said.

Hilary Fordwich, British royals expert, explained that Prince George is continuing the family tradition by attending Eton.

"Just as Prince William attended Eton, it will provide stability, continuity and, given family tradition has proven well for Prince William, it certainly is the best choice given the challenges of raising the future king," Fordwich told Fox News Digital.

Fordwich acknowledged the large media presence for Prince George's first day, she predicts that will die down.

PRINCE WILLIAM AND KATE MIDDLETON 'CAUTIOUS' ABOUT WHICH ROYAL APPEARANCES THEIR CHILDREN MAKE: SOURCE

"While there was extensive coverage of Prince William’s first day, Prince George’s is expected to be more modest with a limited press pool. Given Adelaide Cottage is close by on the Windsor estate, just as Prince William would take tea with his beloved grandmother Queen Elizabeth II, Prince William may well be able to pop home for family visits," she said. "Importantly, being amongst pupils of his ilk he’ll be focused on academics, athletics and relatively normal school-boy adolescent life rather than isolated as previous generations were in the confines of a palace with tutors."

"Luckily, given the family stability, he won’t be subject to the intense media scrutiny his grandparents went through given the state of their marriage when Prince William attended as then-Prince Charles and Princess Diana’s marriage was rapidly disintegrating," Fordwich added.

KATE MIDDLETON IS 'INDISPENSABLE' TO ROYAL FAMILY AS SLIMMED-DOWN MONARCHY FACES MOUNTING PRESSURE: EXPERT

Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital that Prince William and Middleton have consciously made an effort to give Prince George a proper childhood before he becomes the future king.

"I think Prince William and Catherine have been incredibly thoughtful in allowing Prince George to be a child before he has to be a king. Obviously, there is nothing completely normal about being second in line to the throne, but they have surrounded him with routine, family, sports, and school rather than constantly reminding him of his future responsibility," she began.

"Eton is a significant new chapter, but I suspect their priority remains the same," Schofield continued. "George should understand who he is without allowing that title to become his entire identity. "To a degree, yes. But Prince George will never truly be 'just another student,' because everyone knows who he is and what his future holds," she said. The novelty of having a prince in the classroom eventually wears off when everyone has homework due the next morning."

"That could be valuable for Prince George. He needs people around him who will challenge and compete with him. He doesn’t need everyone he meets treating him like a future king," Schofield concluded.

item.description: Joe Thomas built Hall of Fame Farms from five cows and a bull into a 4,100-acre Wisconsin cattle operation focused on raising premium Wagyu beef.
item.content:encoded:
As the new NFL season kicks off on Wednesday night, Pro Football Hall of Fame offensive lineman Joe Thomas is spending much of his time on a different kind of field.

Thomas, the former Cleveland Browns offensive tackle famous for playing an NFL-record 10,363 consecutive snaps, has traded the trenches for tractors and cattle at Hall of Fame Farms, his roughly 4,100-acre operation in Wisconsin.

For Thomas, farming was an ambition long before his playing days were over.

CYCLOSPORA FEARS ARE SENDING SHOPPERS TO FARMERS MARKETS FOR LOCAL PRODUCE

"I grew up outside of Milwaukee, did not grow up on a farm, but always just had a passion for being outside," Thomas said in a recent Fox News interview. "And then when I had the opportunity to go into the NFL, I said if there's only one thing I get out of the NFL, I want to be able to buy my own piece of dirt. I just want to have my own little farm."

Thomas bought the original 1,200-acre property in 2012, while he was still playing for the Browns, and began with just five cows and a bull. Today, the operation encompasses about 4,100 acres, Thomas told Fox News, and raises hundreds of cattle, with an increasing focus on Wagyu beef.

His interest in raising his own food intensified after his 2018 retirement. No longer needing to maintain the massive frame required of an NFL offensive lineman, Thomas said he lost weight and began paying closer attention to nutrition.

"I wanted to try to focus on my health and be more intentional about eating real food," Thomas said. "And, so, I lost about 70 pounds when I retired, and I thought, 'Hey, what a great way to also know where my food came from.'"

Thomas' unusual second career has also attracted attention in Washington.

Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins recently visited Hall of Fame Farms and praised the former NFL star as an example of someone who entered agriculture without growing up in the industry.

"He started with five mama cows and a bull," Rollins said. "So, it's not like he came in and wrote a giant check and became a hobby farmer. Like, he literally built this thing from nothing."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Thomas also joined Rollins at the White House as President Donald Trump signed two executive orders last week aimed at supporting U.S. ranchers.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Wisconsin Farm Bureau Federation for comment.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Thomas hasn't left football entirely. He has continued to work in broadcasting and remains connected to the sport that made him a household name in Cleveland.

But as NFL players begin another season chasing wins on Sundays, Thomas' post-football pursuit is increasingly taking shape hundreds of miles away from an NFL stadium — raising cattle and building the Wisconsin farm he once dreamed about owning.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy attorney's appeal to Trump for pardon could hurt his credibility, expert says
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's defense attorney Kevin Reddington made a surprise appeal to Trump for a pardon after the mistrial, but legal experts are skeptical.
item.content:encoded:
After Lindsay Clancy's criminal defense attorney made a surprise appeal to President Donald Trump for a pardon Tuesday morning, legal experts dismissed the request as unrealistic while questioning the strategy.

"There isn't going to be a pardon for the simple reason there is no mechanism by law which would allow said pardon," said Mark Bederow, a New York City-based criminal defense attorney who has been following the case.

The 36-year-old former nurse faced three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan. After their deaths, she attempted to kill herself and was paralyzed from the injuries. Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial for Clancy Friday after jurors deadlocked following a full week of deliberations.

"This is a very credible, skilled lawyer, and these comments, I think, lack credibility," Bederow told Fox News Digital. "In some level, they lack seriousness because we know it, it's not going to happen — so I don't see the advantage of giving an interview where the only thing people are talking about is Lindsay Clancy's attorney is seeking a pardon or intervention from the president of the United States in the Massachusetts state case."

TRUMP WEIGHS IN ON LINDSAY CLANCY MURDER TRIAL DUBBED 'KANGAROO COURT' BY GOP LEADERS

Clancy attorney Kevin Reddington said Clancy's "life was ruined" after she went to an inexperienced doctor who prescribed medications to treat her postpartum depression in an interview on ABC's "Good Morning America" Tuesday. When asked "what's next" for his client, he appealed directly to the president.

"I'd like to say that perhaps Donald Trump, who felt compelled to speak out about this case, may very well — Mr. President, I would hope that you would consider this young lady the type of the person she is, what she's been through, and consider a pardon," he said.

LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL DECLARED AFTER JURY DEADLOCKS IN KILLINGS OF HER THREE CHILDREN

In a separate interview with Massachusetts' WBZ-TV, Reddington said that while he understands Trump has no grounds to issue a pardon on state charges, he felt that the president could potentially influence the case.

"He certainly has an awful lot of clout, and I'm sure that were he hypothetically to reach out to [Plymouth County District Attorney] Tim Cruz, they're both Republicans, I don't know, maybe that would be something that Tim would listen to and consider," he said. "I think any type of help that we can get is helpful."

LINDSAY CLANCY JUROR ADMITTED 'REASONABLE DOUBT' BUT STILL REFUSED INSANITY VERDICT, FOREPERSON SAYS

item.title: Socialist politicians are 'more racist than the KKK,' says Black Dem official urging voters to ditch El-Sayed
item.description: Karen Whitsett slams Abdul El-Sayed and Democratic Party leaders she says take Black voters for granted, calling out his ties to Hasan Piker.
item.content:encoded:
An elected Democratic official in Michigan is rallying her community against U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and claims those within the socialist rise of her party take Black voters for granted.

"It doesn't change, it's just different slave owners," Democratic Michigan state Rep. Karen Whitsett told Fox News Digital in reference to Democratic Party leaders who believe Black voters are a monolith who should only support left-wing candidates.

She claimed that El-Sayed is not working in the best interest of Black Michiganders and that the far-left wing of her party is "more racist than the KKK."

JASMINE CROCKETT WARNS DEMOCRATS ARE TOO FOCUSED ON WHITE VOTERS, IGNORING BLACK VOTERS

Whitsett called out prominent Black voices known for rallying the community's vote for Democrats — specifically naming Al Sharpton and controversial Detroit pastor Horace Sheffield III, an El-Sayed campaign surrogate. She accused the pair of working to "keep the knee on [Black voters'] neck."

Whitsett said Black voters are "waking up" and are "realizing the power of our vote."

"You can see the serious divide of the crazy socialist far-left and especially the White women," Whitsett said. "They are the worst and the most racist that there possibly ever could be. They're, I think, they're more racist than the KKK."

"Are you trying to help the Black community or are you trying to kill it?" she rhetorically asked. "Are you trying to keep people stupid and ill-informed or what? Because right now I can't tell, right? Is this voter education or are you just trying to make sure you count your slaves on the plantation."

MICHIGAN GOP LAWMAKER CASTS DOUBT ON EL-SAYED’S SOCIALIST DENIAL AS POLICIES TELL ANOTHER STORY: ‘SHARP ODDS’

El-Sayed's values aren't aligned with hers, Whitsett said, adding that she doesn't think he has the best interest of Black voters at heart, either.

"I'm going to stand on Bible first, and I'm going to stand on community first," she said. I don't care about moving up within the Democratic Party. I don't care about making sure my pockets are better."

El-Sayed's campaign did not return Fox News Digital's request for comment on Whitsett's criticism of the candidate and the Democratic Party's leftward shift.

Whitsett is not running for re-election and will retire when her term expires at the end of the year.

"I always try to be a voice of reason, and I'm not a go along, get along. So, my whole thing is it has to make sense, and I am definitely family over party. God over party is of the utmost importance," she said.

"So for me, when you point that out to people, it's just common sense that to people, that's just common sense that El-Sayed is not the candidate," she continued. "There's just no way. It doesn't line up. It doesn't line up Biblically, and it doesn't line up with common sense."

Noting that she does believe everyone should have medical insurance, Whitsett harped on El-Sayed's campaign promise of Medicare for All. She said the progressive candidate hasn't adequately explained how that system will be implemented, and what it means for Americans when they visit the doctor.

EL-SAYED TRIES TO MAKE PEACE WITH JEWISH DEMOCRATS BUT DRAWS LINE AT DUMPING HASAN PIKER

"This Medicare for All, it's not for all. It's not going to change the dynamics of how many doctors there are, or nurses or blood draws or anything else. You're now going to put the government in your health system, and they're going to decide for you."

El-Sayed already finds himself in hot water for palling around on the campaign trail with socialist Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, who said in 2019 that "America deserved 9/11." He has also praised Mao Zedong and Communist China, said capitalists should be murdered in the streets and is known for making antisemitic comments.

El-Sayed has refused to condemn Piker, instead painting him as a "streamer from California" who has no bearing on the race in Michigan, despite inviting Piker to Michigan to campaign for him.

Many Jewish Democrats in Michigan have vowed not to support the far-left candidate, saying in an open letter they feel "threatened and alienated by the politics and allies embraced by Abdul El-Sayed, which has included demonization of Jews, equivocation on terrorism, exclusion of Jewish Americans from public life, and expression of implacable hatred of the world’s only Jewish nation."

item.title: Controversial predictions and rankings of all 32 NFL starting QBs just in time for regular-season kickoff
item.description: Joe Burrow tops the 2026 NFL quarterback rankings while the Atlanta Falcons' Tua Tagovailoa may not even survive as the starter past Week 1.
item.content:encoded:
Finally, settling on a starting quarterback days before the NFL regular-season begins is not a good thing. It's not tactical craftiness to deny the opposition time to prepare, nor is it typically a choice between two good options.

It is a poorly veiled cry for help.

Meet the Atlanta Falcons.

FALCONS NAME SIXTH DIFFERENT WEEK 1 STARTING QUARTERBACK IN SIX YEARS

On Monday, the first day of their week's preparation for a Sunday season-opener at the Pittsburgh Steelers, they announced Tua Tagovailoa as their starter. But beyond that opener?

"I don't think it's fair to really go past this week on anything related to our football team," head coach Kevin Stefanski said.

Left unsaid is Michael Penix Jr. is advancing to a place where he can play in the regular season. So his starter status is looming.

Also unsaid: The Falcons are in some trouble.

The fact is, great teams typically get great quarterback play. It doesn't mean they have great quarterbacks. It means the ones they have play great.

Jalen Hurts is not a great quarterback. But he played great in helping the Philadelphia Eagles win the Super Bowl. Josh Allen is a great quarterback. But he hasn't played well enough, especially not in the playoffs, to get the Bills to a Super Bowl.

Based on that, we celebrate the Wednesday night kickoff of the 2026 NFL season with a ranking of what the league's 32 starting quarterbacks are likely to do in the next five months.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

This is a predictive ranking of which QBs are about to ball and dominate. And which are about to curl up in a ball and disappoint:

32. Jacoby Brissett: He's a fine backup quarterback, but as a starter, he's a fine backup quarterback. 

31. Deshaun Watson: Unless he has a time machine that teleports him back to 2020, this isn't going to go well.

30. Tua Tagovailoa: Might not make it to Week 2 as the starter.

29. Cam Ward: He's growing as a QB, but he's far from full-grown.

28. Malik Willis: The 2026 Dolphins have rejected the idea of surrounding the QB with a good supporting cast and Willis will pay a price for it.

27. Geno Smith: It'll be better than the first NYJ stint (doesn't say much), but not good enough to lift his team above third place in the AFC East.

26. Kirk Cousins: This will work great if Brock Bowers catches 300 passes and Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr. combine for 2,500 rushing yards.

25. Tyler Shough: He's about to turn 27, so the kid gloves developmental period ends or else his replacement comes next season.

24. Jaxson Dart: Over-under on season trips to the blue tent is 4.

23. Bryce Young: Promises more improvement, which means a one-time draft bust might be really good in 2026.

22. Daniel Jones: Good in spurts but never consistently great.

21. Jalen Hurts: Great in spurts, but an excellent team needs him to be more consistently good.

20. C.J. Stroud: The defense is the NFL's best so just don't mess things up.

19. Trevor Lawrence: Last season was excellent but was it his ceiling? 

18. Aaron Rodgers: He needs to make his final NFL season entertaining based on how he plays rather than things he says.

17. Jayden Daniels: The failure to add enough bulk and offensive line injuries is a bad combination for someone wanting to stay healthy.

16. Baker Mayfield: He was supposed to be motivated by his search for a new contract but now must find something else to play angry about.

15. Justin Herbert: He has the arm, the work ethic, the coaching, but has not proven he's got the it-factor in the biggest moments.

14. Jordan Love: Production has declined each of the past two years even as he's been more careful with the ball.

13. Brock Purdy: We saw his ceiling in 2023 and the competition in the NFC West will make it very hard for him to reach that level again this season.

12. Sam Darnold: A good quarterback on an excellent team but it is a huge step to super-stardom.

11. Caleb Williams: If Luther Burden III is healthy and very good, Williams will be great. Otherwise, Williams will be merely good.

10. Bo Nix: Breakout season coming.

9. Kyler Murray: Career season coming.

RAIDERS NAME KIRK COUSINS AS WEEK 1 STARTING QUARTERBACK, FERNANDO MENDOZA WILL BEGIN CAREER AS BACKUP

8. Jared Goff: Underrated by many outside of Detroit, but this guy is consistently outstanding and that isn't likely to change.

7. Drake Maye: Last year was not a mirage. Next stop is super stardom.

6. Lamar Jackson: He can still carry his team, but the Ravens have failed to make the burden lighter so, more of the same.

5. Patrick Mahomes: This rating probably means I must move to Kansas. He remains arguably the NFL's most clutch late-game QB, but the magic of 2020-2022 has faded.

4. Dak Prescott: The only thing stopping him and his offense this year is injuries – or a Jerry Jones impromptu press conference during a drive.

3. Matthew Stafford: Nobody played the position better last season, but it's hard to predict he'll do it again at age 38.

2. Josh Allen: Last season was a bitterly disappointing regression, so a recovery this season is the expectation.

1. Joe Burrow: If he and his offensive teammates stay healthy, they have the best offense and best QB play in the NFL.
